nodes.title: W2-G B1: the cascade speaks Azure Speech DragonHD (server/voice/azureTts.js, streamed raw PCM 24 kHz) whenever AZURE_SPEECH_REGION/_KEY are set (India profile), with the voice per character from CONFIG (server/voice/voices.js: Asha en-IN-Diya, Arjun en-IN-Arjun, Uma en-IN-Meera; TAXILA_CASCADE_ENGINE / TAXILA_DHD_VOICE_<ID> / TAXILA_DHD_RATE_<ID> / TAXILA_VOICES); a DragonHD failure before the first byte (or no headers in 4 s) falls back to the character's gpt-4o-mini-tts voice, logged as an identity change and counted (voice.expr.engine_fallback); the text lane's Hear (/api/tts) speaks the same DragonHD voice

W2-G HV-15: base <prosody rate> -35% for Diya and Arjun (12.3 / 12.2 chars/s on Roman-script Hinglish, inside 11-13); the spec's -25 / -28% was set on a Devanagari line and gives 15.0 chars/s on the Roman text the reply guard writes; Uma unmeasured at -35; owner ear check owed

W2-G B0/B2/B5: the expressive layer is live behind TAXILA_VOICE_EXPRESSIVE (default ON for DragonHD, OFF for gpt-4o-mini-tts, which ignores delivery): seam planDelivery = safety predicate + momentPlan (Moment only, never the verdict for affect) + clause aligner (content law asserted, ≤ 1 filler) → an ENGINE-FREE plan; the governor (per lesson) and the engine compiler run in prewarm/render.js where the lesson and voice are known; per-sentence markers proven silent, per-clause <prosody rate>, pitch -6% on calm/reassuring rows, <break> inside a part, exact silence between parts; every DragonHD document linted (a tag or unproven marker → that part plain)

W2-G B3/B4: the clip bank pipeline and the clip splicer are NOT built (owner: voice-clips-off-and-numbers-normalised). Licensed non-verbals stay in the plan for telemetry and the face; the DragonHD compiler emits none (tags are spoken on en-IN); the Omni compiler writes native tags (benchmark only); BANK_HASH = 'nobank' in every cache key

W2-G: the pause between two TTS parts is EXACT digital silence after trimming the engine's own edge silence (server/voice/expressive/pauses.js edgeTrim: -50 dBFS frames, 30 ms pre-roll kept, ≤ 600 ms dropped at the head, 40 ms tail kept), so the planned pause is the pause heard (plain DragonHD pause SD 0.06 s was the robotic tell); applied only when a plan exists

W2-G: one SSML document per TTS part (splitSentences chunk), not one per reply (HUMAN-VOICE §5.8): keeps the sentence-pipelined first byte and the prewarm lookahead, gives exact pauses between parts and sample-exact clause onsets for the whiteboard; the cost is DragonHD's context across sentence boundaries

W2-G B4: framed TTS v2 on /api/voice/tts-stream when the client sends Accept application/x-taxila-pcm-frames;v=2: [type u8][len u24][payload], 0 PCM, 1 event (clause onsets {clause, part, atSample, atMs}: the whiteboard's clause anchor), 2 header, 3 turn, 4 end; raw audio/pcm for every other client; src/lesson/ttsStream.ts parses it (FrameParser, pcmOfFrames, onTtsEvent) and the default fetchSpeechStream asks for it

W2-G #7: POST /api/lesson/turn-audio calls W2-E's lessonTurn and answers ONE framed response: header {audio: follows|none|rate_limited}, the TurnResponse, the prewarmed reply's PCM, end; client postTurnAudio() resolves the same TurnResponse and parks the audio so the link's next fetchSpeechStream plays it with no request; client flag voice.turnAudio default OFF and the runtime's api.ts turn transport (not W2-G's file) still posts /api/lesson/turn

W2-G deviation: the governor's per-lesson state lives in process memory (LRU 2,000 lessons), not lesson.state.voice: the turn's writer is W2-E's hot file and the seam passes no lesson id; a replica change or restart starts a fresh window (at worst one extra filler, never a floor rule)
W2-G governor: besides ≤ 5 fillers per 10 turns and no repeat within 6, never a filler on two turns in a row (the window rule alone gave 3 fillers in the first 4 turns of a live run)

W2-G: self-corrections (a restarted function phrase in think-aloud) are not generated: a restart is a wording change a child can copy and the owner's rule sends no '...' to the voice; the only inserted word is one governed filler

W2-G: speakable() (server/voice/spoken.js) is the last step before ANY voice: toSpoken, then any digit left read as a plain number in the cell's words, the term lexicon (spoken-lexicon.js TERMS: e.g., i.e., etc., vs, &, w.r.t., approx.), and '...'/'…' as a comma pause; 0 digits and 0 ellipses on 2,000+ kit lines × 4 cells. Interpretation: Hindi number words in the Hindi cells (Hindi mode, Hindi school medium); a Hinglish child with English (or unknown) school medium keeps English number words (NCERT convention, spoken-notation §2.3)
W2-G safety register predicate: moment.safety, a helpline number in the reply, or an identity ANSWER ('not a person', 'insaan nahi'); a greeting that only names her an AI teacher is not a safety turn

W2-G B5 (TEACHER-BRAIN §5.4 L3 synthesis): when the Brain's Moment carries uptakePrelude (W2-E, TAXILA_UPTAKE_PRELUDE=1, off until HV-16), the plan strips the leading echo and the stream plays the child's token first (calm, base rate, 220 ms gap), from a render turn-audio warmed at receipt into the MEMORY cache only (a child's words never reach asset_cache); fail-silent, counted voice.expr.prelude / prelude_miss; deviation: played whenever its audio exists, not only when the reply would land later than 1.2 s

W2-G B7: server/voice/expressive/annotate.js: strict json_schema enum tuples per clause index (never words), validated and clamped to the moment row in code, cached per (text, row, language) in memory + asset_cache, background quota lane; the live seam uses only a MEMORY hit (0 ms); nothing warms it on a live path yet

evals/tts-pace.mjs, centralindia from the US sandbox, n=10 Roman Hinglish teacher lines per cell, plainSsml through azureTts: Diya 0% 19.11, -15% 15.82, -22% 14.96, -30% 13.25, -35% 12.28, -40% 11.13 chars/s (mean); Arjun 18.87 / 16.35 / 14.97 / 13.42 / 12.23 / 11.12; TTFB p50 473 / p90 656 ms (sandbox)

HV-6 run of evals/voice-expressive-nightly.mjs (centralindia, from the sandbox): 80 expressive renders (40 lines × Diya, Arjun; every row; production planner+governor+compiler) transcribed by gpt-4o-transcribe: 0 tag or style words heard (Latin + Devanagari list); marker re-probe 10 markers × 2 voices: 0 spoken; first byte (n=20, not gated outside India) Diya plain p50/p90 449/664 vs expressive 417/429 ms, Arjun 513/747 vs 494/688 ms

evals/voice-expressive-annotate.mjs: taxila-fast effort low, background lane, n=40 kit lines and reply shapes across rows: 40/40 valid after the code validator, 40/40 content preserved, p50 1,220 ms, p90 2,061 ms

seam planDelivery + render (governor + dhd compile + lint) on a 4-sentence think-aloud reply, 1,800 warm iterations standalone: plan p50 0.03 / p99 0.20 ms, render p50 0.06 / p99 0.60 ms (budget ≤ 3 ms p99)

tests/voice-expressive-*.test.mjs: HV-1 2,010 kit lines/reply shapes × 3 voices compile with 0 tags, 0 unproven markers, 0 digits, 0 ellipses, and 0 delivery words in every compiled reply prompt (all characters × lanes); HV-2 2,010/2,010 preserved; HV-3 200 safety fixtures 0 fillers, 0 non-verbals, only [calm], helplines digit by digit, 300 ms between sentences; HV-4 50 seeds × 60 turns in bounds; HV-17 flipping the verdict changes nothing over 5,760 moments; pause realiser exact to 10 ms across chunk sizes 97 B-64 KiB

tests/prod/w2g-voice.mjs against node server/serve.mjs (dist built, Neon test branch, Speech centralindia): 29/29; framed opening (engine dhd, 3 parts, clause onsets 0 / 4,280 / 9,737 ms), raw PCM for old clients, 3 folded turns with audio on the same response (first PCM 2,146-3,022 ms after the request from the US sandbox, not a gate), a disclosure → safeguard with both helplines spoken in the safety register, Hear mp3, 401/400 refusals; account deleted, leftover guardians 4 → 4
scripts/prosody-baseline.mjs --write (centralindia, 3 takes, base rate -35): Diya f0 median 222.2 Hz at 12.67 chars/s; Arjun 136.4 Hz at 12.89 chars/s (alarm ±8% f0, ±12% rate)

Treating any 'AI teacher' self-description as the identity-answer safety register flattened the first-meeting greeting into calm/slow/[calm] in the first live run (row=safety on the opening); narrowed to identity ANSWERS

A 2.5 s header timeout on DragonHD (meant to fall back fast) fired on a cold TLS connection through the sandbox proxy on the first render: in production that is an identity change (another voice) on a healthy service; raised to 4 s and env-tunable
HUMAN-VOICE §12's base rates (-25% Diya, -28% Arjun) on the Roman-script Hinglish the reply guard writes: 15.0 chars/s (n=10 at -22%), above the 11-13 band
The governor's 10-turn window alone (≤ 5 fillers) let 3 fillers into the first 4 turns of a live run (अच्छा, तो, हम्म): a tic at the start of every lesson; a no-consecutive-turns rule was added
